title: Modeling AI-Driven Industry–Education Integration as a Socio-Technical System: A Synergetic Four-Dimensional Collaborative-Efficacy Evaluation Framework
content: Industry–education integration (IEI) is organized as a socio-technical system in which universities, enterprises, students, and artificial intelligence co-produce learning outcomes. Its collaborative efficacy, however, has remained unmeasured, because the elements of the system are assessed in isolation. Grounded in Haken’s synergetics, this paper models AI-driven IEI as a four-dimensional collaborative system (University, Enterprise, Student, and AI; UESA). It defines collaborative efficacy as a super-additive, emergent property rather than a weighted average of parts. The UESA framework operationalizes the system through 27 tertiary indicators aggregated into a single efficacy function V. Indicator weights are set by the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and revised by Bayesian posterior correction as operational data accumulate. The framework is implemented on an operational industry–education integration platform, which couples a large language model (DeepSeek), a job–curriculum knowledge graph, and a topological recommendation engine. In an A/B trial of 3000 undergraduates, enabling the AI layer raised all four system dimensions. The largest gains were in student competency adaptability (+26.0) and AI enablement (+22.9). All 12 key tertiary indicators improved at p < 0.01, and overall efficacy V rose from 64.0 to 83.3. The results indicate that collaborative efficacy in a socio-technical IEI system is measurable and dynamically adaptive, and that it can be decomposed into the contributions of its constituent subsystems.
